note: Independent HEAD re-judgment against RFC 7606 Section 2: "Treat-as-withdraw: In this approach, the UPDATE message containing the path attribute in question MUST be treated as though all contained routes had been withdrawn just as if they had been listed in the WITHDRAWN ROUTES field (or in the MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute if appropriate) of the UPDATE message, thus causing them to be removed from the Adj-RIB-In according to the procedures of [RFC4271]." Read all six tagged units and producers (SynthesizeWithdraw/SynthesizeWithdrawFamilies, applyRFC7606). Positive TestSessionRFC7606ValidUpdateDispatchesAnnouncement sends a conforming eBGP UPDATE over a real session pipe and asserts byte-identical announcement dispatch; negative TestSessionRFC7606TreatAsWithdrawDispatchesWithdrawal sends malformed ORIGIN (len 2) and asserts exact withdraw-only body (withdrawn={0x08,0x0a}, nlri empty, attrLen=0, session Established). Message units TestSynthesizeWithdrawMovesNLRIToWithdrawn and TestSynthesizeWithdrawConvertsMPReachToMPUnreach verify exact legacy IPv4 and MP_REACH-to-MP_UNREACH conversion. RIB units TestRIBTreatAsWithdrawRemovesInstalledRoute and TestRIBTreatAsWithdrawAddPathPreservesPathID verify actual Adj-RIB-In removal (Len 1->0), Loc-RIB BestChangeWithdraw, never-installed no-op, and per-PathID ADD-PATH removal (ID 42 removed, ID 43 retained). Since the prior audit, only the RIB peer-owner key migration (r.bgpPeers[1], ConnectionID=41) and the leading *Session callback parameter in reactor tests changed; all inputs, synthesis calls and exact assertions are intact. Source re-judgment only; no test or gate run claimed.
